note: Elan's Outpost zone notes (written for the Outpost). Notable creatures with source 'classic' were checked against the Classic baseline's spawn points; 'unchecked' = the check could not decide.

zones.name: Durotar
zones.summary: A dry red land on the coast, home of the orcs and the Darkspear trolls. New Horde characters learn the basics here before moving on to the Barrens. Orgrimmar sits at its northern edge.
zones.history: Quilboar once held this land. After the Third War the orcs under Thrall settled it and named it for Thrall's father, Durotan. The Darkspear trolls lost the Echo Isles to the sorcerer Zalazane and built Sen'jin Village on the mainland. The Burning Blade cult still lurks in the hills.

startingFor.note: Darkspear trolls; their early quests lead to Sen'jin Village

mobs.name: Zalazane
mobs.why: Troll sorcerer who drove the Darkspear off the Echo Isles

mobs.name: Sarkoth
mobs.why: Level 4 target of an early quest in the starting area

mobs.name: Gazz'uz
mobs.why: Burning Blade warlock; a known warlock quest target

mentions: Razor Hill: the main Horde town after the starting valley
Sen'jin Village: Darkspear coastal village
Echo Isles: troll starting islands
Tiragarde Keep: old human fort full of hostile mobs
Orgrimmar and Ragefire Chasm are at the north edge

zones.name: Mulgore
zones.summary: Green rolling plains where the tauren live. It is the gentlest Horde starting zone, with small villages and many wild beasts. Thunder Bluff rises on the mesas.
zones.history: The tauren settled these plains after leaving the Barrens, led by Cairne Bloodhoof. Their capital, Thunder Bluff, sits high on the mesas. They honor the Earth Mother and live as hunters. Quilboar and goblins trouble the south.

mobs.name: Baine Bloodhoof
mobs.why: Cairne's son, in the early quests

mobs.name: Arra'chea
mobs.why: Harpy chief, an early quest target

mobs.name: Kyle the Frenzied
mobs.why: Odd wandering rare seen by the Forever client

mentions: Camp Narache: tauren starting camp
Bloodhoof Village: main tauren town
Thunder Bluff: tauren capital
Bael'dun Digsite: goblin dig in the south

zones.name: The Barrens
zones.summary: A huge dry savannah crossed by one long road. Most Horde characters spend their teens here. It holds the Crossroads, Ratchet and two dungeons.
zones.history: The Barrens were green until a long drought dried them. Centaurs, quilboar and raptors now rule much of the land. The orcs built the Crossroads as a base. Goblins run the port of Ratchet. Wailing Caverns and Razorfen Kraul lie on its edge.

mobs.name: Mankrik
mobs.why: Orc whose lost wife starts a famous quest chain

mobs.name: Kreenig Snarlsnout
mobs.why: Quilboar leader near a well-known quest

mentions: The Crossroads: central Horde hub
Ratchet: goblin port with a boat to Booty Bay
Wailing Caverns: dungeon
Razorfen Kraul: dungeon
Camp Taurajo: tauren outpost

zones.name: Alterac Mountains
zones.summary: A cold, rocky range north of Hillsbrad, dotted with ruined human towns and ogre camps. Players come here for mid-level quests, to reach Alterac Valley, and to visit the ruins of a fallen kingdom.
zones.history: Alterac was once a human kingdom that sat between Lordaeron and the northern lands. Its ruler, Lord Perenolde, secretly helped the orcs in the Second War and tried to cover it up by freeing orc prisoners. The other kingdoms cast him out and the land fell apart. Ogres of the Crushridge clan took over the old fortress, and raiders of the Syndicate hide in the hills. Orcs of the Frostwolf clan later settled in the valley beyond, which is why Alliance and Horde now fight there.

mobs.name: Lord Aliden Perenolde
mobs.why: The traitor lord of Alterac, remembered in the ruins and in the Syndicate story.

mobs.name: Mug'thol
mobs.why: Elite ogre chief who rules Crushridge Hold.

mobs.name: Gravis Slipknot
mobs.why: Rare mob in the mountains that hunters and loot hunters look for.

mobs.name: Crushridge Warmonger
mobs.why: Typical tough ogre guarding the hold.

mobs.name: Glommus
mobs.why: Elite mob that wanders the mountains.

mobs.name: Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver
mobs.why: Kirin Tor mage tied to the Dalaran quests in the area.

mentions: Alterac Valley: the huge battleground north of here, where Stormpike and Frostwolf armies fight
Strahnbrad and the Ruins of Alterac: broken towns of the old kingdom
Crushridge Hold: the ogre stronghold with tough elites
Dalaran Crater: where the mage city used to stand before it was lifted away
Ravenholdt Manor: a hidden rogue estate

zones.name: Arathi Highlands
zones.summary: Open grassland and hills in the middle of Lordaeron. Humans, trolls, ogres and orcs all fight over it, which makes it a busy place for quests in the thirties.
zones.history: This was the home of the first human empire, Arathor, whose capital stood here long ago. Later the kingdom of Stromgarde held the land. After the Third War Stromgarde was weak and fell under attack from the Syndicate, ogres and the Witherbark trolls. Prince Galen Trollbane held only a small piece of his own city. Today the Alliance holds Refuge Pointe and the Horde holds Hammerfall.

mobs.name: Prince Galen Trollbane
mobs.why: The last ruler of broken Stromgarde.

mobs.name: Lord Falconcrest
mobs.why: Syndicate leader who hides in a fort near Stromgarde.

mobs.name: Prince Nazjak
mobs.why: Rare spawn that people hunt along the coast south of Stromgarde.

mobs.name: Kenata Dabyrie
mobs.why: Quest giver at Dabyrie's Farmstead, key in the Alliance quests.

mobs.name: Hammerfall Guardian
mobs.why: Strong guards at the Horde town of Hammerfall.

mentions: Refuge Pointe: the Alliance camp
Hammerfall: the Horde camp
Stromgarde Keep: the broken human capital
Witherbark Village and Boulderfist Hall: troll and ogre homes
Arathi Basin: the 15v15 battleground whose entrance is here
Thandol Span: the long bridge south to the Wetlands

zones.name: Badlands
zones.summary: A dry, red canyon land south of Loch Modan, full of ogres, troggs and dwarf diggers. You come here for mid-level quests, the Horde outpost of Kargath, and the Uldaman dungeon.
zones.history: The Badlands hide old titan ruins, and Uldaman is the best known of them. Dwarf explorers dug into it looking for the secrets of their own past. Thrall sent the Kargath Expeditionary Force here to set up the Horde's only outpost in Khaz Modan. Ogres and Dark Iron dwarves hold much of the rest.

mobs.name: Warlord Goretooth
mobs.why: Orc leader of the Kargath Expeditionary Force

mobs.name: Boss Tho'grun
mobs.why: Named ogre boss in the Badlands

mentions: Kargath: small Horde outpost on the northern edge
Uldaman: titan-ruin dungeon entrance in the east (levels 35-45); its first boss Ironaya guards the vault door
Dustbelch Grotto and Angor Fortress: ogre and dwarf strongholds
Mirage Flats: wide desert in the south

zones.name: Blasted Lands
zones.summary: A scarred red wasteland at the far south of the kingdoms, where the Dark Portal stands. Nethergarde Keep guards it. Come here for high-level quests and the fel-ruined Tainted Scar.
zones.history: The Blasted Lands were once the southern part of the Black Morass swamp. Demonic magic from the Dark Portal dried them into a barren wasteland during the First War. Nethergarde Keep was built later to keep watch on the portal. Demons under Lord Kazzak gather at the Tainted Scar, and Dreadmaul ogres roam the desert.

mobs.name: Lord Kazzak
mobs.why: Giant demon world boss waiting at the Tainted Scar

mobs.name: Razelikh the Defiler
mobs.why: Elite demon lieutenant, killed at the Rise of the Defiler

mentions: Nethergarde Keep: Alliance fort beside the Dark Portal
The Tainted Scar: ridge where Kazzak stands
Dreadmaul Rock: ogre fortress in the north
Dark Portal: the gate that leads to Outland
Fallen Hero of the Horde: ghost at the swamp border who starts a long quest chain

zones.name: Tirisfal Glades
zones.summary: A gloomy, misty forest of farms and graveyards. This is where new Forsaken characters begin, with Brill as the first town.
zones.history: Tirisfal was a calm farming region just outside the old capital of Lordaeron. The plague and the Scourge turned it into a land of the dead. After Arthas destroyed the kingdom, some undead broke free from the Lich King and became the Forsaken under Sylvanas. They took the ruins of Lordaeron and built the Undercity below it. The Scarlet Crusade still holds the northeast with their monastery.

mobs.name: Dark Cleric Duesten
mobs.why: Priest trainer in Deathknell; one of the first NPCs undead players meet.

mobs.name: Executor Zygand
mobs.why: Quest giver in Deathknell for early quests.

mobs.name: Apothecary Johaan
mobs.why: Quest giver near Brill in the plague-research story.

mobs.name: Captain Melrache
mobs.why: Elite-level boss of the Scarlet camp at Garren's Haunt.

mobs.name: Alexi Barov
mobs.why: Head of the House of Barov, linked to the Scholomance story.

mentions: Brill: the main Forsaken town
Deathknell: the Undead starting village
Scarlet Monastery: the dungeon entrance in the far northeast
Ruins of Lordaeron: the entrance to the Undercity
Agamand Mills and Garren's Haunt: spooky farms with quests

zones.name: Silverpine Forest
zones.summary: A dark pine forest south of Tirisfal. It is the second stop for Forsaken players, full of worgen rumors, Scarlet raiders and the dungeon Shadowfang Keep.
zones.history: Silverpine was once a quiet forest on the edge of Lordaeron, watched over by the nearby mages of Dalaran. During the Third War, the wizard Arugal summoned worgen to fight the orcs and they turned on him and the land. Shadowfang Keep became his lair. The Forsaken now fight the worgen and the Alliance from the Sepulcher, their base in the north.

mobs.name: Archmage Ataeric
mobs.why: Mage from Dalaran in the forest who gives quests.

mobs.name: Deathstalker Faerleia
mobs.why: Forsaken ranger leader at the Sepulcher.

mobs.name: Ivar the Foul
mobs.why: Worgen-related quest villain at Pyrewood area.

mobs.name: Moonrage Whitescalp
mobs.why: Common Moonrage worgen in the forest.

mobs.name: Fenrus the Devourer
mobs.why: First boss of Shadowfang Keep, the dungeon entered from here.

mentions: The Sepulcher: the Forsaken base
Shadowfang Keep: the dungeon at the forest's heart, level 22-30
Pyrewood Village and Ambermill: lost villages
Quests about the worgen curse and Dalaran rescue

zones.name: Western Plaguelands
zones.summary: A ruined, plague-struck land of dead farms and old Lordaeron villages. Levelers and dungeon runners come here for undead hunting and for the Scholomance dungeon.
zones.history: This was once the farming heartland of Lordaeron. Arthas spread the plague of undeath here, and the villagers turned into the walking dead. Andorhal fell first, and ever since it has been a Scourge stronghold. The Argent Dawn now trains fighters to keep the plague from spreading further. Dark necromancers, the Cult of the Damned and the Scarlet Crusade all fight for ground.

mobs.name: Araj the Summoner
mobs.why: Necromancer boss in Andorhal tied to a quest chain.

mobs.name: Weldon Barov
mobs.why: Barov family member with a long quest chain.

mobs.name: Commander Ashlam Valorfist
mobs.why: Argent Dawn commander at Chillwind Camp.

mentions: Scholomance: the necromancer school dungeon at Caer Darrow
Andorhal: ruined town with the Scourge
Chillwind Camp: the Alliance-friendly camp
Hearthglen: Scarlet Crusade fortress
Sorrow Hill and Felstone Field: famous quest areas

zones.name: Eastern Plaguelands
zones.summary: A dead, haunted land that is the last big zone before level 60. It is full of undead, plague beasts and the entrance to Stratholme and Naxxramas.
zones.history: The Eastern Plaguelands are the heart of Lordaeron's fall. Stratholme was the first city to be touched by the plague, and Arthas purged it here. The Scourge floated their necropolis, Naxxramas, over the land. The Scarlet Crusade and the Argent Dawn, an alliance of Horde and Alliance heroes, fight for the rest. Light's Hope Chapel is the Argent Dawn's last stand.

mobs.name: Tirion Fordring
mobs.why: Fallen paladin who becomes a key hero of the Light.

mobs.name: Lord Maxwell Tyrosus
mobs.why: Leader of the Argent Dawn in the field.

mobs.name: Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff
mobs.why: Argent Dawn leader at Light's Hope Chapel.

mobs.name: Betina Bigglezink
mobs.why: Argent Dawn quest giver at the chapel.

mentions: Light's Hope Chapel: base of the Argent Dawn
Stratholme: the dungeon here, split into two halves
Naxxramas: the raid hanging over the zone
Corin's Crossing and Terrordale: undead towns
Scourge Invasion: world event that sends the dead into other zones

zones.name: Hillsbrad Foothills
zones.summary: Green hills and farmland with two rival towns, Southshore for the Alliance and Tarren Mill for the Horde. Players meet each other and fight over quests and kills.
zones.history: Hillsbrad was a farm region of Lordaeron. The land was spared in the Third War but fell to Syndicate raiders and the Dalaran exiles. Durnholde Keep, once an internment camp for orcs, stands on the hill. The Forsaken took Tarren Mill from the humans, and Southshore stayed human. The two towns have fought ever since.

mobs.name: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle
mobs.why: Alliance officer giving early Hillsbrad quests.

mentions: Southshore and Tarren Mill: the rival towns
Durnholde Keep: entrance to the Old Hillsbrad dungeon
Southshore vs Tarren Mill: a well known world PvP fight
Syndicate and Dalaran quests

zones.name: The Hinterlands
zones.summary: A thick jungle-forest in the north-east of the Eastern Kingdoms. The Wildhammer dwarves and the Horde-friendly Revantusk trolls live here, along with hostile Witherbark and Vilebranch trolls.
zones.history: The Hinterlands are the home of the Wildhammer dwarves, whose clan built Aerie Peak. They share the land with troll tribes that go back to the Amani empire. The Vilebranch trolls hold the city of Jintha'Alor and serve the old blood god. The Revantusk trolls joined the Horde, while the Wildhammer joined the Alliance. Their wars over this valley are what the quests tell about.

mobs.name: Mith'rethis the Enchanter
mobs.why: Rare elite known for rare drops.

mobs.name: Falstad Wildhammer
mobs.why: High thane of the Wildhammer at Aerie Peak.

mentions: Aerie Peak: the Wildhammer town
Revantusk Village: the Horde troll village
Jintha'Alor: Vilebranch troll city
Seradane: a green dragon in the northwest
The Overlook Cliffs and Skulk Rock

zones.name: Dun Morogh
zones.summary: A snowy mountain land and the homeland of the dwarves and gnomes. It is where new dwarf and gnome characters start, with Ironforge just inside.
zones.history: Dun Morogh holds Ironforge, the dwarf capital, and the old gnome city of Gnomeregan. Gnomeregan was overrun by troggs and then poisoned by the traitor Mekgineer Thermaplugg, so the gnomes fled to Ironforge. The dwarves have kept the peace of the mountains for a long time, but Frostmane trolls and troggs keep trying to move in. The Alliance defends the land from Kharanos.

mobs.name: Great Father Arctikus
mobs.why: Famous rare bear in the snow.

mobs.name: Balir Frosthammer
mobs.why: Coldridge Valley trainer in the starting area.

mobs.name: Senir Whitebeard
mobs.why: Quest giver for new players in Dun Morogh.

mobs.name: Jarven Thunderbrew
mobs.why: Brewmaster tied to the brewing quests.

mobs.name: Mekgineer Thermaplugg
mobs.why: The villain behind the Gnomeregan disaster.

mentions: Kharanos: the main town after Coldridge Valley
Ironforge: the dwarf capital at the center
Gnomeregan: the poisoned gnome city dungeon
Coldridge Valley: the first valley for dwarves and gnomes
Frostmane trolls and Rockjaw troggs

zones.name: Searing Gorge
zones.summary: A burning rocky gorge at the foot of Blackrock Mountain. Dark Iron dwarves hold forges and fortresses here. Go for forge and Thorium Brotherhood quests and to enter Blackrock Depths.
zones.history: About 230 years ago the Dark Iron sorcerer-thane Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros in the War of the Three Hammers. The eruption made Blackrock Mountain and blackened the gorge. The Dark Iron later dug the Cauldron and its Slag Pit, worked by captured slaves. The Thorium Brotherhood, a Dark Iron splinter group, set up Thorium Point to watch them.

mobs.name: Kalaran Windblade
mobs.why: Quest giver of the Divine Retribution chain

mobs.name: Dark Iron Taskmaster
mobs.why: Slave driver found across the gorge

mentions: Thorium Point: fort for both factions, hub for the Thorium Brotherhood
Blackrock Mountain: next door, holds Blackrock Depths, Blackrock Spire, Molten Core and Blackwing Lair
The Cauldron and the Slag Pit: Dark Iron strongholds
Key to Searing Gorge: the Alliance entrance from Loch Modan was locked in Classic and needed a key quest

zones.name: Burning Steppes
zones.summary: A hot ash-covered land beside Blackrock Mountain. Blackrock orcs and black dragon forces rule it. You go for high-level quests and the way up to Blackrock Spire.
zones.history: Dark Iron dwarves first settled the Burning Steppes after leaving Ironforge, and Thaurissan's summoning of Ragnaros melted the mountains into the Blackrock volcano. Orcs settled here in the First War, and the Horde used Blackrock Spire as a base in the Second War. Orgrim Doomhammer killed Anduin Lothar near the volcano late in that war.

mobs.name: Ragged John
mobs.why: Old man at Morgan's Vigil with a dragon story

mobs.name: Grark Lorkrub
mobs.why: Orc prisoner at Blackrock Stronghold with a Horde escort quest

mobs.name: Gor'tesh
mobs.why: Brute lord of the Firegut ogres, an Alliance quest target

mentions: Morgan's Vigil and Flame Crest: Alliance and Horde camps
Blackrock Spire: dungeon above the zone, ending with Warchief Rend Blackhand
Dreadmaul Hold and Altar of Storms: giants and dragons
Lord Victor Nefarius and Nefarian: black dragon story behind the Onyxia and Blackwing attunements

zones.name: Elwynn Forest
zones.summary: The green home of Stormwind. It is peaceful, with farms, lakes and mines, plus a few bandit, gnoll and kobold camps.
zones.history: Stormwind was founded around 1,200 years before the Dark Portal opened, and Elwynn became the heartland of the human kingdom. Orcs invaded in the First War, and Lothar's knights drove them back through the forest. Goldshire and Moonbrook were the last towns to fall. Today the army guards the roads, but gnolls, bandits and murlocs still trouble the farms.

startingFor.note: Dwarf and Gnome start in Dun Morogh instead.

mobs.name: Hogger
mobs.why: Famous gnoll elite near Elwynn's roads

mobs.name: Princess
mobs.why: Rare boar with a fun solo kill

mobs.name: Marshal Haggard
mobs.why: Retired guard leader at Eastvale Logging Camp

mentions: Goldshire: main village and crossroads
Northshire Abbey: the human starting valley
Fargodeep Mine and Goldtooth's Den: kobold mines
Eastvale Logging Camp and Westbrook Garrison: the army posts on the east and west edges
Stormwind City: the Alliance capital just northwest

zones.name: Deadwind Pass
zones.summary: A gloomy mountain pass leading up to Karazhan, the tower of a mad mage. There is little to do but kill ogres and see the sights.
zones.history: Deadwind Pass runs between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows. The wizard Aegwynn built Karazhan, and her son Medivh lived there. He died at the hands of Lothar and Khadgar, which left a fel blight on the land. Ogres have since settled the pass, with mounds in the Vice.
mentions: Karazhan: tower on the hill, closed to players in Classic
Morgan's Plot: ruined farm
The Vice: canyon where the Deadwind ogres live
Sleeping Gorge and Deadman's Crossing
zones.foreverNotes: Karazhan is not open to players in Classic.

zones.name: Duskwood
zones.summary: A dark, spooky forest full of undead, spiders and worgen. Darkshire is the hub. Go for a creepy quest chain and the road south to Stranglethorn.
zones.history: Duskwood was once called Brightwood. In the First War the Horde raided the area, and Medivh's death spread fel energy that changed it into the dark Duskwood. The necromancer Morbent Fel then filled the woods with undead, and Defias agents hid in the dark. Darkshire is guarded by the Night Watch.

mobs.name: Stitches
mobs.why: Giant abomination who walks toward Darkshire

mobs.name: Eliza
mobs.why: Bride of the embalmer, a spooky quest villain

mobs.name: Morbent Fel
mobs.why: Necromancer behind much of the undead

mobs.name: Mor'Ladim
mobs.why: Elite skeleton in Raven Hill Cemetery

mobs.name: Commander Felstrom
mobs.why: Rare undead in the Dawning Woods Catacombs

mobs.name: Lord Malathrom
mobs.why: Rare ghoul in the Dawning Woods Catacombs

mobs.name: Abercrombie
mobs.why: Hermit who starts the Stitches quests

mentions: Darkshire: central town, ruled by Lord Ello Ebonlocke
Raven Hill Cemetery
Twilight Grove: the Emerald Dream portal
Manor Mistmantle and Yorgen Farmstead
Road east into Deadwind Pass and south to Stranglethorn Vale

zones.name: Loch Modan
zones.summary: A green, rainy dwarf land around a big lake, east of Dun Morogh. Good for levels 10-20 with quests about troggs, ogres and bears.
zones.history: Loch Modan was built by the dwarves of Ironforge after the Second War, who dammed the river to make the loch. The Stonewrought Dam is its famous work. Dark Iron dwarves, troggs and the Mo'grosh ogres hit the dwarves again and again. The Thelsamar townsfolk have stayed brave through all of it.

mobs.name: Grawmug
mobs.why: Rare mob that levelers hunt in the zone.

mobs.name: Ol' Sooty
mobs.why: Rare elite mob in Loch Modan.

mobs.name: Mo'grosh Ogre
mobs.why: Typical elite ogre at the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

mentions: Thelsamar: the main town
Stonewrought Dam: the big dwarf-built dam
Mo'grosh Stronghold: an elite ogre cave
Ironband's Excavation Site and the trogg digs
Dun Algaz and the road to the Badlands

zones.name: Redridge Mountains
zones.summary: A hilly red region around a big lake. Lakeshire is the Alliance town. Go for Blackrock orc and gnoll quests.
zones.history: Dark Iron dwarves founded a colony in the north, and their thane summoned Ragnaros, who made Blackrock Mountain. Orcs conquered the Redridge Mountains in the First War. Later Blackrock raiders, an orc warlock named Morganth and the Shadowhide gnolls took the eastern half. Lakeshire's militia holds the lake shore.

mobs.name: Lieutenant Fangore
mobs.why: Shadowhide gnoll general in the east, party of five advised

mobs.name: Marshal Marris
mobs.why: Lakeshire quest giver at the bridge

mentions: Lakeshire: main town
Stonewatch Keep and Tower
Render's Valley: Blackrock orc camps
Alther's Mill and Three Corners
Black dragon quests
zones.foreverNotes: The Warcraft Wiki Forever map comparison marks Redridge as substantively changed on the map, without saying how.

zones.name: Stranglethorn Vale
zones.summary: A huge jungle full of trolls, tigers, raptors and pirates. Booty Bay is the neutral port. It is a classic leveling zone with many kills and quests.
zones.history: The Gurubashi trolls ruled the vale until a civil war, driven by priests of Hakkar the Soulflayer, broke their empire. The Zandalari beat Hakkar at Zul'Gurub, and the surviving Atal'ai priests fled to the Swamp of Sorrows. Goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel took Booty Bay from the trolls. Pirates, ogres and rebels have fought over the jungle since.

mobs.name: King Bangalash
mobs.why: Famous white tiger rare in Northern Stranglethorn

mobs.name: Mokk the Savage
mobs.why: Gorilla rare at the Spirit Den in the Cape

mobs.name: Colonel Kurzen
mobs.why: Elite jungle fighter under the Mind's Eye

mobs.name: Hemet Nesingwary
mobs.why: Hunter who runs the big game quests

mobs.name: Mosh'Ogg Warmonger
mobs.why: Elite ogre at the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound

mobs.name: Commander Aggro'gosh
mobs.why: Horde commander at Grom'gol Base Camp

mentions: Booty Bay: neutral port with boats to Ratchet and Menethil
Nesingwary's Expedition: hunting quests
Grom'gol Base Camp and Rebel Camp: faction camps; the rebels fight Kurzen
Zul'Gurub: raid entrance in the north, the old Gurubashi capital
Gurubashi Arena: PvP arena near Booty Bay
zones.foreverNotes: Reports say Stranglethorn gains a new dungeon, The Drowned City (levels 35-40), tied to submerged ruins off the coast.

zones.name: Swamp of Sorrows
zones.summary: A wet, marshy land near the Dark Portal. The sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar sits in the swamp. Go for orc and troll quests and the Sunken Temple dungeon.
zones.history: The swamp was once the northern part of the Black Morass. The Atal'ai trolls built a temple here after the Gurubashi empire fell, and the green dragonflight sank it into the bog. The orcs built Stonard in the First War, and the swamp was named for those who died in the Second War.

mobs.name: Itharius
mobs.why: Green dragon ambassador who sends you into the temple

mobs.name: Fallen Hero of the Horde
mobs.why: Ghost at the Blasted Lands border who starts a long quest chain

mentions: Stonard: Horde town
Temple of Atal'Hakkar: Sunken Temple dungeon entrance in the east; the prophet Jammal'an leads the Atal'ai
Splinterspear Junction and Misty Reed Farm
Itharius's cave: starts the green dragon quest chain

zones.name: Westfall
zones.summary: Rolling farmland in the far west, plagued by the Defias Brotherhood. The Deadmines dungeon lies beside the coast. Good for quests from level 10.
zones.history: Westfall was Stormwind's breadbasket until the Defias Brotherhood took over. The Defias began as stonemasons who were never paid for rebuilding Stormwind. Their leader Edwin VanCleef made the Deadmines his base. The People's Militia, later the Westfall Brigade, pushed back and helped end the Brotherhood there.

mobs.name: Foe Reaper 4000
mobs.why: Rare harvest golem on the farms

mobs.name: Old Blanchy
mobs.why: Beloved farm horse and quest giver

mentions: Sentinel Hill: main outpost
Moonbrook: former mining town above the Deadmines
Deadmines: dungeon for levels 15-21, ending with Edwin VanCleef
Alexston Farmstead and The Dead Acre: harvest golem fields
Defias Brotherhood quest chain

zones.name: Wetlands
zones.summary: A grey swampland on the sea, with Menethil Harbor as the main town. You go here to fight Dragonmaw orcs and to take boats to Auberdine and Theramore.
zones.history: The Wetlands used to be the home of the proud dwarves of Khaz Modan. During the Second War, orcs of the Dragonmaw clan held red dragons captive and raided here. The Alliance freed them, but the clan is still dangerous at Grim Batol. The swamps lie below the Thandol Span, a bridge the dwarves built to the north.

mobs.name: Ormer Ironbraid
mobs.why: Dwarf quest giver in the swamp.

mentions: Menethil Harbor: the boat port
Grim Batol: the old dragon fortress
Dun Modr and Dragonmaw Fortress
Thandol Span: the long bridge north to Arathi
Boats to Auberdine and Theramore

zones.name: Teldrassil
zones.summary: A green island forest that grows on the branches of a giant tree. It is calm and pretty, with gentle early quests. Night Elves begin their journey here.
zones.history: Teldrassil is a young world tree, planted by the night elves after they lost their first great tree long ago. The druids grew it to give their people a new home and a link to nature. Its branches hold the capital Darnassus above the waves. Corruption has crept into some of its animals and satyrs, and Cenarion druids work to heal it.

startingFor.note: Dolanaar is the next town on the road.

mobs.name: Githyiss the Vile
mobs.why: Early rare spider that low-level hunters seek

mobs.name: Lady Sathrah
mobs.why: Rare spider queen in the north

mobs.name: Lord Melenas
mobs.why: Satyr leader listed among the island's notable foes

mobs.name: Melithar Staghelm
mobs.why: Druid who gives early quests near the start

mobs.name: Conservator Ilthalaine
mobs.why: Starts the corruption quests near Aldrassil

mobs.name: Tenaron Stormgrip
mobs.why: Druid trainer and quest giver near Dolanaar

mobs.name: Gnarlpine Ambusher
mobs.why: Furbolg tribe that attacks you on the road

mentions: Shadowglen: the Night Elf starting valley
Dolanaar: first real town
Aldrassil: the great tree at the island's heart
Rut'theran Village: the dock where ferries leave for Darkshore
Portal to Darnassus: the tree trunk leads up to the capital

zones.name: Darkshore
zones.summary: A long, foggy coast north of Ashenvale. Auberdine is the only travel hub and the base for most quests. You deal with corrupted furbolgs, murlocs, naga and dark cultists.
zones.history: Darkshore was once one of the richest parts of the night elf empire, with great cities like Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran. The Great Sundering destroyed much of the coast. After the Third War the night elves came back and revived the port of Auberdine. Today furbolgs have turned feral, and the Cult of the Dark Strand and the Twilight's Hammer lurk in hideouts.

mobs.name: Thundris Windweaver
mobs.why: Leader of the Alliance effort on the coast

mobs.name: Terenthis
mobs.why: Auberdine quest giver who starts the furbolg corruption chain

mobs.name: Lady Vespira
mobs.why: Rare spider; Wowhead lists her in Darkshore

mobs.name: Grimclaw
mobs.why: Strong Darkshore bear that quest hunters seek

mobs.name: Onu
mobs.why: Ancient in the Grove of the Ancients worried about the Twilight's Hammer

mentions: Auberdine: the only travel hub and an Alliance night elf village
Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran: ruins of old night elf cities
Tower of Althalaxx: a quest-chain landmark
Grove of the Ancients: where the Twilight's Hammer lurks at the Master's Glaive
Boat link to Rut'theran Village in Teldrassil

zones.name: Ashenvale
zones.summary: A big, old forest the night elves guard, now fought over by the Horde. Expect many quests on both sides and open-world fights. Warsong lumber camps and forest bosses make it busy.
zones.history: Ashenvale has been a night elf homeland for thousands of years. The Burning Legion and satyrs have corrupted parts of the forest, and the Horde has cut timber to feed its war effort. The night elves resist from Astranaar and other posts. The zone is contested, with constant fights between Alliance and Horde.

mobs.name: Raene Wolfrunner
mobs.why: Ruler of the Alliance side in Astranaar

mobs.name: Delgren the Purifier
mobs.why: Leads the fight against the Shadow Council from Maestra's Post

mobs.name: Dal Bloodclaw
mobs.why: Villain of an Ashenvale quest chain

mobs.name: Kayneth Stillwind
mobs.why: Night elf commander in Forest Song

mobs.name: Je'neu Sancrea
mobs.why: Zoram'gar Outpost quest giver for Blackfathom Deeps

mentions: Astranaar: main Alliance hub, ruled by Raene Wolfrunner
Splintertree Post and Warsong Lumber Camp: Horde logging bases
Blackfathom Deeps: dungeon in the northwest corner on Zoram Strand
Bough Shadow: elite micro dungeon where a Dragon of Nightmare can appear
Forest Song, Maestra's Post and Zoram'gar Outpost: smaller quest camps

zones.name: Thousand Needles
zones.summary: A canyon land with tall stone spires. The Shimmering Flats hold a goblin and gnome racetrack. Tauren and centaurs fight over the rocks.
zones.history: Gnomes and goblins built the Mirage Raceway on the flats to settle which race builds better. Tauren from Freewind Post fought the Grimtotem and the centaur clans. Razorfen Downs, a dungeon, sits near the border.
mentions: Freewind Post: tauren quest hub
Mirage Raceway: goblin and gnome racetrack
Highperch: wyvern nests
Shimmering Flats: salt flats
Razorfen Downs: dungeon nearby

zones.name: Stonetalon Mountains
zones.summary: A rocky range between the Barrens and the north. Both factions have posts here. Goblin loggers and night elf druids fight over the forests.
zones.history: The mountains once held a fountain of health blessed by Elune. In the Third War it was corrupted, then cleansed by Thrall and Cairne. Later the goblin Venture Company cut the forests and mined the rock.

mobs.name: Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle
mobs.why: Gnome engineer targeted in a quest

mentions: Sun Rock Retreat: Horde town
Windshear Crag: Venture Co. mining area
Grimtotem Post: neutral camp
Charred Vale: burnt valley with dragons
Stonetalon Peak: ruined mountaintop

zones.name: Desolace
zones.summary: A barren land of dust, ruins and centaur camps. It holds Maraudon, a big dungeon. Both factions fight cultists and rival centaur clans.
zones.history: Desolace was once green grassland. Tauren shamans woke the earth spirit Theradras, who drained the land. She and Zaetar fathered the centaur, who drove out the tauren. The Horde joined the Magram and slew Theradras in Maraudon.

mobs.name: Warug
mobs.why: Magram leader friendly to the Horde

mentions: Shadowprey Village: Darkspear village on the coast
Ghost Walker Post: tauren camp
Nijel's Point: Alliance outpost
Maraudon: dungeon with three wings
Kodo Graveyard

zones.name: Feralas
zones.summary: A thick jungle with ogres, gnolls and sea creatures. Dire Maul is hidden here. Each faction holds a camp.
zones.history: Feralas was once part of the night elf lands, and old elven ruins remain. Gordunni ogres broke into Dire Maul. The Alliance holds Feathermoon Stronghold on an island. The Horde friend Camp Mojache sits inland.
mentions: Feathermoon Stronghold: Alliance island fort
Camp Mojache: tauren camp
Dire Maul: dungeon in the north
Tower of Estulan: ruined tower
Gordunni ogre caves

zones.name: Dustwallow Marsh
zones.summary: A misty swamp with Theramore, the human port in Kalimdor. Onyxia's Lair sits in the northwest. Dragons and ogres roam the mud.
zones.history: After the Third War Jaina Proudmoore founded Theramore here. The orcs of Brackenwall Village are close by. Onyxia, daughter of Deathwing, lairs in a cave. The marsh is full of old ruins.

mobs.name: Onyxia
mobs.why: Dragon boss of her own raid

mentions: Theramore Isle: human port
Brackenwall Village: Horde camp
Mudsprocket: neutral goblin town
Onyxia's Lair: raid entrance

zones.name: Tanaris
zones.summary: A vast desert on the south coast with the goblin town Gadgetzan. Zul'Farrak and the Caverns of Time are here. It is a main leveling zone for the 40s.
zones.history: Tanaris was once greener. Troll tribes left the ruined city Zul'Farrak. Gadgetzan was built as a neutral trade city. Bronze dragons guard time in the Caverns of Time. Pirates and elementals roam the dunes.

mobs.name: Anachronos
mobs.why: Bronze dragon of the Caverns of Time

mentions: Gadgetzan: neutral goblin town
Zul'Farrak: troll dungeon
Caverns of Time: bronze dragon caves
Lost Rigger Cove: pirate cove

zones.name: Azshara
zones.summary: A rocky coast of ruined elven lands, with goblin, orc and Alliance camps and few quest hubs. Lake Mennar is an elite area. Players go for the dragon Azuregos, the shark Maws and rare targets.
zones.history: Azshara was part of the night elf capital Zin-Azshari. The city fell in the War of the Ancients and much of it sank into the sea. The region is named for Queen Azshara, whom demonic influence drove mad. Ruins, naga and hydras fill the coast today. The blue dragon Azuregos still guards the south.

mobs.name: Maws
mobs.why: Giant shark boss summoned in the Bay of Storms

mobs.name: Magus Rimtori
mobs.why: Leads a Thalassian expedition for Highborne relics

mentions: Valormok: Horde town
Talrendis Point: Alliance camp
Grim Ulang: orc trading village
Lake Mennar: elite micro dungeon
Bay of Storms: naga, sea giants and Hetaera's Clutch
Duke Hydraxis lives on a small island far to the east

zones.name: Felwood
zones.summary: A forest twisted by demon corruption, north of Winterspring. Quests are grindy and tough. You come for rare animals and the corrupt grove of Jaedenar.
zones.history: Felwood used to be a lovely forest like Ashenvale. Demonic corruption poisoned its trees and animals, and the Scourge and surviving demons from the Third War settled here. Cenarion druids at Emerald Sanctuary try to heal it. The Shadow Council rules Jaedenar from Shadow Hold.

mobs.name: Lord Banehollow
mobs.why: Shadow Council leader in Shadow Hold

mentions: Emerald Sanctuary: Cenarion camp
Jaedenar and Shadow Hold: the Shadow Council's base
Timbermaw Hold: furbolg base and tunnel to Winterspring
Deadwood Village, Felpaw Village, Jadefire Glen and Bloodvenom Post: smaller camps
Bloodvenom Falls: cursed waters

zones.name: Un'Goro Crater
zones.summary: A lost crater full of dinosaurs, giant plants and fire elementals. Quests send you into the wild to collect and hunt. It is a great place for levels 50 to 55.
zones.history: Un'Goro was shaped by the titans and is full of ancient life. It stays warm and wet from the volcano at its center. Marshal Expeditions run camps to study the creatures. Strange crystals and hive insects live here too.

mobs.name: Tyrant Devilsaur
mobs.why: Elite devilsaur that roams the middle

mobs.name: Blazerunner
mobs.why: Fire elemental elite in Fire Plume Ridge

mentions: Marshal's Refuge: neutral camp
Fire Plume Ridge: volcano in the center
The Slithering Scar: bug land
Golakka Hot Springs: crystals
Terror Run: dinosaur plains

zones.name: Moonglade
zones.summary: A small, peaceful druid valley around Lake Elune'ara. The only land way in is through Timbermaw Hold. Druids visit Nighthaven to train, and everyone can come for quests and the Lunar Festival.
zones.history: Cenarius lived in Moonglade in ancient times, and the Cenarion Circle was founded there. In the Third War Tyrande retrieved the Horn of Cenarius here to wake Malfurion. After that, Moonglade opened to every druid race, and Keeper Remulos became its guardian. Moonglade Wardens keep the peace between races.

mobs.name: Dendrite Starblaze
mobs.why: Teaches druids bear and aquatic form

mobs.name: Omen
mobs.why: Sleeps in Lake Elune'ara and wakes for the Lunar Festival

mentions: Nighthaven: the main druid town
Lake Elune'ara: sacred lake with fish
Shrine of Remulos: where Remulos tends the emerald dragons
Stormrage Barrow Dens: druid sanctums with a portal to the Dreamway
Lunar Festival: yearly event here

zones.name: Silithus
zones.summary: A dry desert full of insects, south of Un'Goro. The gate to Ahn'Qiraj opens here. You go for end-game quests and bug hives.
zones.history: After the War of the Shifting Sands, the Qiraji were sealed behind the Scarab Wall, but their silithid servants spread across southern Kalimdor. The night elves later reopened the gates of Ahn'Qiraj. The Cenarion Circle now watches the hives from Cenarion Hold. The bronze dragonflight has returned, and patch 1.12 added world PvP over Silithyst.

mobs.name: Commander Mar'alith
mobs.why: Cenarion Hold commander, searching for his missing wife

mobs.name: Highlord Demitrian
mobs.why: Sends top heroes after Prince Thunderaan

mobs.name: Prince Thunderaan
mobs.why: The wind lord heroes are sent to defeat

mobs.name: Twilight Marauder Morna
mobs.why: Twilight's Hammer leader at their camp

mobs.name: Twilight Keeper Exeter
mobs.why: Twilight's Hammer cultist in the camps

mobs.name: Rutgar Glyphshaper
mobs.why: Dwarf explorer at the Bronzebeard Encampment

mobs.name: Fandral Staghelm
mobs.why: Archdruid seen at the Scarab Wall

mobs.name: Merithra of the Dream
mobs.why: Green dragon of the gate event

mentions: Cenarion Hold: main hub of the Cenarion Circle
The Scarab Wall and Gates of Ahn'Qiraj
Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj (20-man) and Temple of Ahn'Qiraj (40-man): raids
Hive'Ashi, Hive'Regal and Hive'Zora: silithid hives
Twilight camps: Base Camp, Outpost and Post
Bronzebeard Encampment and Valor's Rest

zones.name: Winterspring
zones.summary: A cold snowy peak area above Felwood. It has the neutral town Everlook and tough groups of frost trolls and bears. Great for the last levels before 60.
zones.history: Winterspring is a cold mountain land where Winterfall furbolgs have gone mad and dragonkin and demons haunt the gorges. The goblin town of Everlook is the neutral hub. Elite demons in Darkwhisper Gorge guard a blocked way to Hyjal.

mobs.name: Lady Hederine
mobs.why: Rare elite succubus in Darkwhisper Gorge

mentions: Everlook: goblin capital and flight point
Starfall Village: Cenarion-friendly village
Mazthoril: elite area with dragon lairs
Winterfall Village: furbolg camp
Darkwhisper Gorge and Frostwhisper Gorge: elite areas
Frostsaber Rock and Frostfire Hot Springs
zones.foreverNotes: WoW Forever's own Winterspring map lists levels 53-60.

zones.name: Stormwind City
zones.summary: The human capital and a major Alliance hub. It has the auction house, bank, class trainers and many gates. The Stockade lies in its canals.
zones.history: Stormwind was razed by the orcs in the First War, and King Llane was killed. The Stonemasons' Guild rebuilt it and built the Deeprun Tram to Ironforge. Unpaid guild workers rioted, a queen died by accident, and the guild turned into the Defias Brotherhood. After King Varian Wrynn went missing, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon ruled for his young son Anduin. Lady Prestor is secretly the black dragon Onyxia.
mentions: The Stockade: prison dungeon in the canals, entered from the Mage Quarter
Trade District, Cathedral Square, Old Town
Mage Quarter, Valley of Heroes and Dwarven District
Stormwind Harbor with boats to Darnassus and Auberdine
Deeprun Tram to Ironforge
zones.foreverNotes: The Warcraft Wiki Forever map comparison marks Stormwind as substantively changed on the map, without saying how.

zones.name: Orgrimmar
zones.summary: The Horde capital, a fortress in the cliffs of Durotar. Trainers, a bank, an auction house and the leaders are here. Ragefire Chasm lies below.
zones.history: Thrall founded Orgrimmar after leading the orcs to Kalimdor. He named it for the old warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. The city is built of wood and spikes in a stone valley. A fire cult has settled the caverns beneath.
mentions: Valley of Strength: main hub
Valley of Spirits: shaman quarter
Ragefire Chasm: dungeon entrance
Cleft of Shadow: warlock and rogue quarter

zones.name: Ironforge
zones.summary: The dwarf capital, built into a mountain. It has a big forge hall, tinkers' quarter, a tavern, a bank and an auction house. Dwarves, gnomes and other Alliance players use it as a home.
zones.history: Ironforge was built by the Bronzebeard clan long ago and has stood through many wars. It was home to the Council of Three Hammers and survived the Dark Iron War. King Magni Bronzebeard rules it. Gnomes found shelter here after the fall of Gnomeregan. Today it is a safe place for Alliance players.

mobs.name: Royal Historian Archesonus
mobs.why: Quest giver for the Ironforge lore.

mentions: The Deeprun Tram: underground rail to Stormwind
The Great Forge
Tinker Town: gnome quarter
The Mystic Ward: mages and priests
The Hall of Explorers

zones.name: Thunder Bluff
zones.summary: The capital of the tauren, built on mesas above Mulgore. Rope bridges link the bluffs. Elders live in the high lodges.
zones.history: Cairne Bloodhoof led the tauren to these mesas as a safe home. The city is open and has no walls. The Grimtotem tribe plots against the Bloodhoofs. The Great Tree honors the Sun Spirit.
mentions: Elder Rise: chiefs' district
Spirit Rise: spirit healers
Hunter Rise: hunter trainers
Lower Rise: shops

zones.name: Darnassus
zones.summary: The Night Elf capital, up in the branches of Teldrassil. Trainers, shops and the Temple of the Moon are here. It is calm and green.
zones.history: Darnassus is the night elf capital, grown in the branches of Teldrassil. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind rules from the Temple of the Moon. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids from the Cenarion Enclave. A portal in the Temple Gardens takes you to Rut'theran Village.
mentions: Temple of the Moon: home of the Sisters of Elune and the city's leaders
Cenarion Enclave: druid and hunter trainers
Warrior's Terrace: city gate, forge and training dummies
Temple Gardens: bank and portal to Rut'theran Village
Tradesmen's Terrace: Auction House
Craftsmen's Terrace: inn and mailboxes

zones.name: Undercity
zones.summary: The capital of the Forsaken, built in the sewers under Lordaeron. It has trainers, banks, an auction house and the Apothecarium.
zones.history: The Undercity was a series of sewers and crypts under the capital of Lordaeron. After Arthas destroyed the city, the Forsaken made it their home. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner rules from the Royal Quarter and plans to take back the lands above. The Royal Apothecary Society studies plague cures there, as well as other dark experiments.

mobs.name: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner
mobs.why: The Banshee Queen and ruler of the Forsaken.

mentions: The Apothecarium: plague labs
The Royal Quarter: Sylvanas's court
Trade Quarter: bank and auction
The Rogues' Quarter
Zeppelin tower to Orgrimmar

zones.name: Mount Hyjal
zones.summary: A max-level zone that is new to WoW Forever, high in northern Kalimdor. You go there for endgame quests, reputations, world events and two new raids. You walk in from Winterspring through Darkwhisper Gorge.
zones.history: Hyjal has always been sacred ground of the Wild Gods and the night elves. After the Sundering, Illidan made a new Well of Eternity on its peak, and the World Tree Nordrassil was planted over it. In the Third War, the demon Archimonde marched on the mountain and was beaten in a great final battle, which cost the night elves their immortality. Malfurion then sealed the mountain away. In Forever the forest is slowly healing, and the story is said to involve the Wild Gods and dangers left behind.

mobs.name: Nythus the Dreambound
mobs.why: Final boss of the Hyjal Summit raid (20 players)

mobs.name: Sonya Darkhallow
mobs.why: Final boss of the Barrow Deeps raid

mentions: Hyjal Summit: new 20-player raid with 13 listed encounters
Barrow Deeps: new raid under the mountain (wiki says 10 players); opened together with Onyxia's Lair
Darkwhisper Gorge: the way in, east of Winterspring
Subzones include Summit of Eternity, Shrine of Aviana, Malorne's Retreat, Cradle of Tranquility and Felblood Scar
Cenarion Circle quests and max-level world events are said to be based here
zones.foreverNotes: The whole zone is Forever-only (vanilla Hyjal was closed). Added in 1.60.1. Raids unlock after launch (wiki: 9 December, with Onyxia's Lair). The player's quest cache holds no Hyjal quests yet, so story details are not confirmed.

zones.name: Zephras Isle
zones.summary: A floating island in Skywall, the elemental plane of air, and the home of the new Skyborne race. Every Skyborne character starts here and levels to about 12 before sailing to Azeroth. The main town is Valanaar, with airships from the Valanaar Skydocks.
zones.history: Long ago, Highborne exiles made a pact with the wind spirits and built a society in Skywall. They became the Skyborne, who call themselves shen'dorei. Centuries ago the air spirits vanished, and the magic holding the islands up is fading. Other islands have broken apart, refugees crowd onto Zephras, and the people are split: the Windshapers want to find and restore the spirits, while the High Order wants to stand on its own with arcane power.

startingFor.note: Both Skyborne variants start here at level 1. First quests: 'Coming of Age' (talk to Rorian the Dayseeker) and 'Harmony in Balance' (thin out the young vuldren east of the village). The Skyborne race needs the Skyborne Heroic or Epic Pack.

mobs.name: Rorian the Dayseeker
mobs.why: Leader of Thendal Village; gives new Skyborne their first tasks

mobs.name: Ayessa Dawnsinger
mobs.why: Grand Skyseer of the Windshapers (Horde side leader)

mobs.name: Elaadrin Evengale
mobs.why: Supreme Magister of the High Order (Alliance side leader)

mobs.name: Juvenile Vuldren
mobs.why: First creatures you hunt, east of Thendal Village

mobs.name: Ventaari Brightwish
mobs.why: Windshapers figure with quotes on the wiki's Zephras page

mentions: Valanaar: the island's main town; airships go to Dalaran/Alterac (Alliance) and Mulgore (Horde)
Thendal Grove and Thendal Village: the Skyborne starting area
Shen'dar Village, Falaath Village and the Shrine of Akir: smaller settlements
Ruins of Ban'aethal, Sanctum of Storms and the Bandit Hideout: places to explore and fight
Non-Skyborne players can also do the Zephras intro quests (per a GM post reported by Icy Veins)
zones.foreverNotes: Entirely new in WoW Forever (patch 1.60.1); not in Classic or retail.

zones.name: Riverglades
zones.summary: A big new contested zone on the east coast of the Eastern Kingdoms, east of the Badlands and Burning Steppes. It fills the mid-level gap with many quests and a lot of world PvP. A neutral goblin port links it by boat to Tanaris.
zones.history: The valley was once Stormwind land. In the First War the orcs raided the town of Sunnyglade and enslaved the people there, until soldiers freed them and rebuilt it. The Horde later took the region, and Stormwind gave it up to defend its home. Now the people of Farholde Keep, led by Demar Brant, fight to win it back, while the Horde holds its own camps.

mobs.name: Knight Commander Demar Brant
mobs.why: Leads the Alliance at Farholde Keep

mentions: Krol'dok Stronghold: new 5-player dungeon, levels 40-45 (first listed as 40-55, later corrected)
Farholde Keep: the Alliance base and flight point
Rog'mar and Bolder'ok: Horde bases
Powderfuse Port: neutral goblin port with a boat to Tanaris
Sunnyglade: the old human town from the First War story
zones.foreverNotes: Entirely new in WoW Forever (patch 1.60.1); opens at full launch. Developers mentioned over 150 quests. Wildlife and foes listed on the wiki include gnolls, murlocs, ogres, crocolisks and harvest golems; Twilight's Hammer is also present. No Riverglades quests are in the player's quest cache yet.

zones.name: Shen'dralas
zones.summary: A hidden valley in central Kalimdor, between Desolace, Mulgore and Feralas, full of old Highborne ruins. It carries on the centaur clan story from Desolace. You enter from Desolace through the Valley of Bones.
zones.history: Shen'dralas is tied to the Shen'dralar, the Highborne of Dire Maul. In the player's quests, the Gelkis centaur send you after the rival Magram, who are raising very old, two-legged skeletons in the cursed Valley of Bones. The scout Nerlokh waits at the valley's southern entrance and suspects the Magram's necromancers are not what they seem. Bristleback quilboar also live in the area.

mobs.name: Undead Ravager
mobs.why: Risen skeletons in the Valley of Bones; target of 'Ravaging Ravagers'

mobs.name: Magram Necromancer
mobs.why: The Magram casters behind the undead; 'Outing Outcasts' has you take their garb

mobs.name: Nerlokh
mobs.why: Gelkis scout and quest giver at the Valley of Bones

mentions: Valley of Bones: the cursed way in from Desolace
Gelkis vs Magram quest chain (Gelkis reputation; ends with an attack on Khan Jehn)
Bristleback Retreat, Outcast Hideaway, Evenshade's Overlook, Magram Front and Forlorn Gardens: subzones
Links to the Shen'dralar of Dire Maul (Prince Tortheldrin)
zones.foreverNotes: Entirely new in WoW Forever (patch 1.60.1). The level range is not official: the wiki says unknown, Gfinity says 45-53, and the cached quests are level 38-40 (from 35). The Valley of Bones, a Desolace subzone in Classic, is filed under Shen'dralas in Forever's area data.
